steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A market is any opportunity for buyers and sellers to interact to establish price — physical or virtual.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Factor markets trade factors of production (labour market, capital market). Product markets trade finished goods and services to consumers.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The price mechanism allocates resources: rising prices signal shortage, attracting producers; falling prices signal surplus, driving producers away. Functions: signalling, rationing, incentivising.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Primary sector extracts raw materials (farming). Secondary manufactures goods (factories). Tertiary provides services (retail, finance). The UK is ~80% tertiary.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between factor markets and product markets, giving an example of each. | Describe the three functions of the price mechanism in allocating resources. | Analyse why the UK economy has shifted from secondary to tertiary sector dominance.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always distinguish factor markets from product markets: factor = inputs, product = outputs. The price mechanism has three key functions: signalling, rationing, incentivising. Use all three. When discussing sector shifts, link to BOTH causes AND consequences.
